Alex — thanks, that helps a lot. I put together two quick scenarios below (high level) and attached committed-use terms.

Scenario A — Startup program (if eligible)
- 12 months at 50% off standard hosted rates (applies to both embeddings + generation), soft cap up to 250M tokens/mo for the discount window.
- Example blended unit economics: if standard rate is $70 / 1M tokens blended, 50% off -> ~$35 / 1M tokens (this aligns with your target).

Scenario B — Committed-use tiers (public hosted pricing + commitment discounts)
- 3mo commitment: 10% discount on list; good for small pilots
- 12mo commitment: 25%–40% discount depending on $/month commit; typical breakpoint to get to ~$25–$30 / 1M is a committed spend of ~$25k+/mo (example depends on exact token mix)
- 24mo / multi-year: additional 5–10% incentive vs 12mo and price protection for growth; available for deals with predictable ramp and enterprise procurement

Rough modeled example (blended):
- No commit: $70 / 1M -> at 120M tokens = $8,400 / month (this is illustrative; our list varies by model and mix)
- 12mo commit (mid tier): target blended $28 / 1M -> at 120M tokens = $3,360 / month (requires commensurate monthly commitment; I’ll model your ramp to show how this changes over time)

Next steps I propose:
1) You: confirm startup eligibility (I can send the application checklist)
2) Me: I’ll run a 12–24mo committed-use model using your 120 -> 350–400M ramp and show target $/1M and monthly spend bands (will include multi-year incentive line)
3) If the model looks good, we can put together a formal quote and start a procurement timeline (Ben is cc’d for finance/terms).

I’ll attach redwood-committed-use-terms.pdf with the common breakpoints and an example worksheet. If you want we can hop on Friday — I’m free 10–11am PT.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
